NDT consulting for Sacramento-area companies: written practices, procedures and audits under California rules

Sacramento-area inspection companies, fabricators and plant owners use outsourced ASNT NDT Level III consulting to keep a written practice current, write and approve NDT procedures, examine and certify technicians, and prepare for client audits and subcontractor approvals. Atlantis does that work remotely from Houston and on site when an examination or audit needs it, with an ASNT NDT Level III named on the documents.

California's regulators, and what sits outside NDT consulting. Three regimes touch an NDT company working around Sacramento, and only one of them is the Level III's to manage:

  • Workplace safety: California runs its own OSHA-approved State Plan, Cal/OSHA, covering most private-sector employers. Its rules apply to field crews, but safety programs are the employer's responsibility, not part of a Level III engagement.
  • Boilers and pressure vessels: the Pressure Vessel Unit of the Department of Industrial Relations' Division of Industrial Safety and Health is the state authority. NDE on repairs and alterations feeds the records its inspectors and the repair organization keep, so procedures must name the code and acceptance criteria that apply.
  • Radiography: California is an NRC Agreement State, so radioactive material licensing and radiographer requirements are set by the state program. That license and its radiation safety program are separate from the NDT written practice, and a consultant should say so rather than blur them.

What Sacramento clients usually ask a Level III for. Common engagements are a written practice review against the current SNT-TC-1A edition and the client's contract terms; procedure writing and approval for UT, MT, PT, VT, RT and ET; general, specific and practical examinations for Level I and II candidates, with vision examination records; and preparation for a customer audit. Companies bidding to owners and EPC contractors in the Central Valley may be asked to pass a subcontractor approval audit, and the same checklist works in reverse for owners who hire NDT contractors: written practice, certification files with documented hours, procedure qualification records, instrument and reference block calibration, and evidence that the named Level III actually reviews the work.

How the work is delivered. Document work, procedure review and audit preparation run remotely, with drafts marked up and returned against an agreed date. Practical examinations and on-site audits are scheduled as visits when they are needed.

Start with outsourced ASNT NDT Level III consulting, NDT procedure development or SNT-TC-1A training program setup. Certification and calibration records can be kept audit-ready in Atlantis ERP certificate tracking, and technicians can train through Level II training. California-wide detail is on the NDT consulting in California page. To scope an engagement, send your written practice, methods and audit dates through the Sacramento consulting request.
